terms.gloss: a league, an alliance; a partnership
evidence: Caes. BG 6.2: Ambiorīgem sibi societāte et foedere adjungunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The alliance itself, between states, kings or people; also any partnership or association (see organization). Allies are sociī.
The treaty that makes the alliance; foedus facere (icere), to make a treaty.
Our formation, for a modern thing the reference works do not name: an association of teams (turma, the house word for a team; see team). The contest itself is a certāmen (see competition).

phrases.latin: Ambiorīgem sibi societāte et foedere adjungunt
phrases.english: they bind Ambiorix to themselves by a league and a treaty
to form an alliance with someone
to conclude an alliance (a treaty) with someone

phrases.latin: societās ad bellum dēfendendum atque īnferendum facta

sources: Lewis & Short: societas · Lewis & Short: foedus · Lewis & Short: turma
Caesar, Sallust and Cicero as Lewis & Short quotes them.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 185–188, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
